security_problem: A valid tools/call can reach the downstream stdio or remote transport even when its final allow event was never durably appended to the hash-linked JSONL audit ledger: Logger.Log swallows write/short-write errors and advances chain state before the write is known to have succeeded, and all three terminal allow branches forward unconditionally after best-effort logging.
required_behavior: For every valid tools/call C, downstream_transport_received(C) implies a full, hash-linked EventToolAllowed record for C completed on the configured regular O_SYNC JSONL ledger before the downstream write began. Logger.CommitAuthorization accepts only terminal allow events, requires a regular durable sink, performs a full-write check, poisons the logger on write/short-write failure, and advances hash-chain state only after success. Approved, explicit, and default/fallback allow branches commit before returning "forward"; any commit failure produces a generic client deny and zero stdio/remote relay. Metrics and session taints mutate only after commit success. Omitted/invalid AuditLogPath fails closed.
failure_behavior: Fail closed: sink failure, short write, closed logger, non-durable sink, or poisoned logger denies the valid tools/call with no relay on either transport.
